title: Classifying (x+1)/(x-1)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Show that f(x)=(x+1)/(x-1) is neither even nor odd.

steps.title: Evaluate at -x
steps.explanation: Negating the input and clearing the common minus sign from numerator and denominator gives (x-1)/(x+1).
steps.why: Multiplying top and bottom by -1 does not change a fraction.

steps.title: Test Evenness
steps.explanation: The two expressions disagree, e.g. f(2)=3 but f(-2)=1/3, so f is not even.
steps.why: Cross-multiplying would force x^2-1 to equal itself only when the swap is trivial, which fails for x=2.

steps.title: Test Oddness
steps.explanation: The right side is negative and equals -f(x); at x=2 it is -3, different from f(-2)=1/3, so f is not odd.
steps.why: One counterexample invalidates the identity f(-x)=-f(x).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.explanation: Neither symmetry identity holds, so the hyperbola y=(x+1)/(x-1) has no y-axis or origin symmetry.
steps.why: Failing both defining identities is precisely the 'neither' case.
